q: 1. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation is the process of rotating the plane table so that all lines on the plotted sheet remain parallel to their corresponding lines on the ground.

q: 2. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 3. Locating the position of a plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: The three-point problem is the specific technique of orienting a plane table and fixing the instrument's own station by resection with reference to three known, plotted points.

q: 4. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 5. Which one of the following procedures for getting accurate orientation is the most distinctive feature of the art of plane tabling
explain: Resection (particularly the two-point and three-point problems) is considered the most distinctive and skill-demanding feature of plane table surveying, used to orient the table accurately.

q: 6. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is
explain: In an optical square, the two mirrors (horizon glass and index glass) are fixed at 45 degrees to each other, causing the incident ray to be deflected through 90 degrees via double reflection.

q: 7. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: Radiation is the method in which rays are drawn from a single plane table station to each visible (accessible) point, and distances are plotted to scale along these rays, all from one setup.

q: 8. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: chances to miss details are less.
explain: Because plotting is done in the field itself while the ground is in view, there is little chance of any topographic detail being missed, which is a key advantage of plane table surveying.

q: 9. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Points that are inaccessible (cannot be reached to measure distance) but are visible from two known plane table stations are plotted using the intersection method.

q: 10. Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
explain: Non-horizontality of the plane table board is an instrumental (equipment set-up) error, as distinct from personal errors like defective sighting, orientation, or centering.

q: 11. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in
explain: The deflection angle method of traversing is commonly used across all types of linear engineering works - canals, highways, and railways - since it directly gives the angle by which the alignment changes at each station.

q: 12. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in
explain: Locating an unknown point C by measuring/computing angles or distances from two known points A and B on a fixed baseline, and plotting by intersection, is the basic principle of triangulation.

q: 13. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table board used in surveying is typically 750 mm x 900 mm in size.

q: 14. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of
explain: Both the two-point problem and three-point problem are specific techniques used to solve the resection problem in plane table surveying - determining the plane table's own position from known points.

q: 15. The plotting of small areas which can be commanded from a single station, is usually done on the plane table by the method of
explain: When a small area can be entirely observed and measured from one single station, the method of radiation is used to plot all the points directly from that station.

q: 16. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing the instrument stations only, is a
explain: Resection is specifically used to locate/establish the plane table's own instrument station with reference to already plotted points.

q: 17. Intersection is preferred to radiation when
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: Intersection is preferred over radiation specifically when the points to be located are inaccessible, so their distance cannot be directly measured, requiring rays from two known stations instead.

q: 18. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

q: 19. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

q: 20. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

q: 21. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

q: 22. Three point problem is concerned with
explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

q: 23. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

q: 24. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

q: 25. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

q: 26. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

q: 27. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

q: 28. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

q: 29. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

q: 30. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

q: 31. The orientation of the table is done by
explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

q: 32. "Fiducial edge " is the working edge of
explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

q: 33. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: When orienting a plane table at a station using only two known but inaccessible points, the specific technique used is the two-point problem, a form of resection using two references.

q: 34. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: Compared to the three-point problem, the accuracy of the 'fix' obtained by the two-point problem is generally not as reliable, since it involves an iterative trial-and-error graphical solution.

q: 35. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest divisions of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernier scale divided by total number of divisions of primary scale
explain: The least count of a vernier is defined as the value of one division of the main (primary) scale divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale.

q: 36. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: For surveying a small area commanded from a single station, radiation is one of the most important (and simplest) plane table operations used for setting up detail plotting.

q: 37. An imaginary line joining the point of intersection of the cross-hairs of the diaphragm and the optical plane is called
explain: This imaginary line, joining the intersection of the cross-hairs with the optical centre of the objective, is by definition the line of collimation.

q: 38. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob attached) is the specific instrument used to accurately centre a plane table exactly over a ground station mark.

q: 39. The plane table surveying is
options: most suitable for preparing small-scale maps
less costly that a theodolite survey
explain: Plane table surveying offers multiple advantages together - it is suited for small-scale mapping, works well in areas with magnetic disturbance (since it doesn't rely on compass bearings), and is generally less costly than theodolite surveys - so all of the above apply.

q: 40. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground is called
explain: This operation of rotating the plane table so plotted lines remain parallel to corresponding ground lines is, by definition, orientation.

q: 41. In plate tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distance directly is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly during plane tabling without separate chaining.
